# Torsion bar re-indexing for ride height

> **[Unverified]** This page rests on a single community report. Cross-check before relying on it.

> Items marked **[Partial]** are only partly confirmed by the source and need more work. They stay in the review queue and are firmed up, corrected or removed as more sources come in.

## Summary

[Partial] Re-index torsion bars by adjusting ride height at door seams to achieve a 1 to 1.5 inch front-to-rear rake. [t1849]

## Procedure

> **[Partial]** Needs more work: the verifier could confirm only part of this procedure (the steps marked [Partial], or whether the list is complete). Steps or precautions may be wrong or missing; read the source thread before relying on it. Later runs fill it in as more sources are found.

1. Ensure tire pressure is even on all four corners.
2. [Partial] Measure the ride height at the seams below the doors, aiming for a front-to-rear rake of 1 to 1.5 inches with the front lower.
3. Support the front of the vehicle under the differential using a floor jack.
4. Loosen the top nut on the adjuster lever just barely with a 19mm open end wrench.
5. [Partial] Remove the adjuster bolt from below by rotating it counter-clockwise while lying on your back looking up at the car.
6. Mark where the adjuster lever sits relative to the cross member prior to full removal.
7. [Partial] Clean the removed adjuster bolt with a wire brush and apply anti-seize lubricant where necessary.
8. Hit the adjuster finger towards the rear of the vehicle with a hammer to knock the torsion bar forward out of the lower control arm anchor.
9. [Partial] Rotate the torsion bar while keeping the adjuster lever attached, ensuring splines are coated in anti-seize before re-inserting it into the anchor.
10. Secure both anchors by tapping the end of the bar with a hammer to ensure they sit firmly in place.
11. Slide the hardware back in, then turn the bolt until the adjuster finger rests within the cross member.
12. Check the ride height at the seams on each side and make fine-tuned adjustments until even.

_Procedure reported by [t1849]. Photos of this job are in the source: <https://www.xterranation.org/index.php?threads/how-to-re-index-your-torsion-bars.2813/>_

## Tools

- Floor jack [t1849]
- [Partial] 19mm open end wrench [t1849]

## Tips & gotchas

- [Partial] Measure bump stop gap with a 0.5 inch clearance as the target limit. [t1849]
- Use anti-seize on torsion bar splines before re-inserting to prevent binding next time. [t1849]

## Common mistakes

- [Partial] Failing to relieve weight from the differential support, causing uneven adjustment. [t1849]
- [Partial] Rotating too far and having adjuster levers hang below or hit the back of the cross member without room for more lift. [t1849]
